newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling weakens marginally against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling weakens marginally against dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling weakened marginally against the dollar just off a record low on Tuesday as market sentiment stayed low because of economic and political worries.
The shilling which opened at 69.68 on Tuesday compared to 69.99 at Monday's close eased marginally to close at 69.86 on Tuesday as investors got into the market to buy dollars at cheap levels.
"There is nothing to look forward to. The shilling is still weak," a dealer told Reuters. "The shilling is trading in a range. It looks like the 70-level is a hard psychological level to break."
The shilling hit its official record low against the dollar on Monday of 70.68 before firming slightly before the close.
Commercial bank dealers said the market had become very unpredictable as investors mulled over their next move after a series of political and economic blows to Kenya since May.
Investors hold some five billion shillings of treasury bills which they opted not to roll over on Thursday at the Central Bank of Kenya treasury bill auction, citing uncertainty.
"It will depend on what they decide to do with it. How they get out if they decide to, will affect the shilling," a dealer said.

Pre-election violence and the blacklisting of Kenya by the cancellation of an International Monetary Fund loan package and the subsequent delay of a World Bank disbursement dented the country's image and jolted confidence in the emerging market.
The shilling has depreciated a total of 17.41 percent since the IMF cancelled a $205 million aid package to Kenya on July 31, citing corruption.
But while foreign investors counted their losses from the shilling's depreciation, exporters rejoiced.
Coffee and tea officials said the immediate and direct beneficiaries of the weak shilling was the farmer who is paid in dollars for his produce.

"The auction is all done in dollars. The shilling's depreciation will have a very distinct bearing on the producer he has to pay for his expenses in shillings," Norman Wilson, managing director of Africa Tea Brokers told Reuters.

Commercial bank dealers who had positioned themselves for a firm shilling on Tuesday morning said dollar inflows -- of up to $2 million from Tuesday's weekly coffee auction did nothing for the battered currency.

On Monday, market analysts said violence in Mombasa, Kenya's largest tourist centre undermined chances of a shilling recovery as tourism was Kenya's biggest source of hard currency, earning $465 million in 1996.

Tour operators said they had received some cancellations and Italy and Germany warned their tourists to take precautions in the coast region, where at least 35 people have been killed since Wednesday.
Police blamed the Mombasa attacks on thugs, but pamphlets have cited ethnic slogans for seizing regional power in general elections due later this year. No date for the poll has yet been set.
